stemMd: What does “money tied up in inventory” mean?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Money physically locked inside the valve.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Funds committed to stored items and unavailable for other uses.

options.label: C
options.textMd: A tax charged on every hour of machine use.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Money that has disappeared without any asset remaining.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Cash earned only when machines stop.

explanationMd: Purchasing spare parts commits funds to assets sitting in storage. Those funds cannot simultaneously be spent elsewhere. “Tied up” describes that opportunity cost, not literal imprisonment of cash.

distractorRationale.a: The phrase is financial, not literal containment.
distractorRationale.e: The passage concerns capital committed to stock.
distractorRationale.d: The funds are represented by stored parts.
